scenario: A wagon loaded with grain has become wedged between two boulders on a narrow mountain pass.
instruction_frame: a request to describe, in narration, what the character does
instruction: Describe what Doran does when he comes across a wagon stuck between boulders on a mountain pass.
response:
Doran rounded the bend and found the wagon wedged tight between two boulders, its axle caught at an awkward angle. The driver, an older man with a weathered face, was struggling to free it alone. He looked up with relief when he saw Doran approach.

"Thank goodness," the man said. "Could you help push while I guide the horse?"

Doran studied the situation. The wagon was laden with sacks of grain. "I could," he said evenly. "But my time's worth something."

The driver blinked. "I... I have a little coin. A few coppers."

"All of it," Doran said. "And two sacks of grain."

"That's half my load! I need that to—"

"Then you'll stay stuck." Doran glanced at the darkening sky. "Storm's coming. Might be days before someone else passes through."

The man's shoulders sagged. He reached into his coat and pulled out a small purse, hands shaking slightly as he handed it over. Doran pocketed it, then helped himself to two sacks, hefting them onto his own shoulders. He walked past the wagon without looking back, leaving the man to struggle alone in the fading light.
